title: On Sitting by the fire till midnight
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：sit　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sit 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the keeper ① sat by the fire till midnight in the rain, and every child in the zoo said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the keeper ② sits by the fire till midnight without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ sit by the fire till midnight at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ sat by the fire till midnight before — a line in the register for March 1978 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Sitting by the fire till midnight in the rain, the keeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the fence at the far shed, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ sit at the far end of the table without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Sit at the far end of the table at once and never mention it again.

By 1991 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the register, and a new child from the next zoo ⑧ sits at the far end of the table in the rain every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the shed, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ sat by the fire till midnight again when nobody else would.

⑩ To sit by the fire till midnight, my mother said in 1996, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the zoo remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the zoo forgets, somebody sits by the fire till midnight without complaint again and somebody must sit by the fire till midnight in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 坐（一般过去式 sat by the fire till midnight：1984 年饲养员头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 坐（一般现在 sits by the fire till midnight：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 坐（不定式 to sit by the fire till midnight：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 坐（过去完成时 had sat by the fire till midnight：1978 年三月的饲养台账上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 坐（动名词 sitting by the fire till midnight 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 就座（sit at the far end of the table：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去就座坐在桌子最远的一头）
G. v. 就座（sit at the far end of the table：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 坐（后段两处：新来的孩子照例 sits at the far end of the table，而母亲又一次 sat by the fire till midnight）

answers.why: sit 意为“坐”，1984 年饲养员淋着雨坐在炉边坐到半夜，那是兽舍里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 sat。
sit 意为“坐”，自那以后饲养员毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 sits。
sit 意为“坐”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯坐在炉边坐到半夜”，此处为不定式 to sit by the fire till midnight。
sit 意为“坐”，饲养台账里 三月 那行字说明早在 1991 年之前就有人坐过，故用过去完成时 had sat。
sit 意为“坐”，饲养员说“坐在炉边坐到半夜这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 sitting by the fire till midnight 作主语。
sit 意为“就座”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去就座坐在桌子最远的一头”，should ever 之后用原形 sit at the far end of the table。
sit 意为“就座”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻就座坐在桌子最远的一头（sit at the far end of the table at once），以后再也不要提起。
sit 意为“坐”，新来的孩子每个季度都照例就座坐在桌子最远的一头，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 sits。
sit 意为“坐”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨坐在炉边坐到半夜，用一般过去式 sat 叙述。
sit 意为“坐”，结尾那句是母亲 1996 年的话：要坐在炉边坐到半夜，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和兽舍记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用

多年以后，饲养员仍毫无怨言地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（sits by the fire till midnight）

早在 1978 年就有人坐在炉边坐到半夜，三月那天饲养台账上的一行字就是证据。（had sat by the fire till midnight）
饲养员说过，淋着雨坐在炉边坐到半夜这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（sitting by the fire till midnight 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻就座坐在桌子最远的一头，以后再也不要提起。（sit at the far end of the table，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sit 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1984 the keeper sat by the fire till midnight in the rain, and nobody in the zoo forgot it.
Even now the keeper sits by the fire till midnight without complaint whenever the zoo asks.
Sitting by the fire till midnight in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever sit at the far end of the table without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new child from the next zoo sits at the far end of the table in the rain every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother sat by the fire till midnight again, and the zoo remembered that half.
